title: The climb to 3D: bets on the staircase
learning_goal: See the PhD proposal as a staircase of test benches and the data factory that will feed it; separate what is guaranteed by construction from what must be measured; read each upper step as a bet written down before the data exist, with its criterion, its confidence and the question to settle before computing.
takeaway: Some properties are guaranteed by construction; everything else on the staircase is a bet written down before the data exist, with the criterion that will settle it.
notes: Status (D4): 10.3, 10.4 and 10.5 were PROVISIONAL in the outline and are now pending (no CPU run); 10.7 and 10.9 pending; 10.1, 10.2, 10.6, 10.8, 10.9-bridge and ch10.Q ready. Every pending scene ships as an empty seat with a READY anchor (10.3 E2 reference map, 10.4 E3 ghost, 10.5 Taylor-Green cells and a SCHEMATIC growth curve, 10.7 lamp panel, 10.9 VKS and DRESDYN drawings), the bet, CONFIDENCE, the criterion with its source and an ASK box; seat types vary: curve (10.3, 10.4), map (10.5, 10.9 VKS), lamps (10.7), curve (10.9 DRESDYN). Seat ASK boxes: 10.3 'Is the 2D tier at 128² worth its GPU hours, or go straight to 3D?'; 10.4 D17 'Add runs at Rm 17.25, 17.5 and 17.75 to pin the edge?'; 10.5 D18 'Near the threshold: lengthen runs to saturation, or flag and exclude them?'; 10.7 'To test criterion (c), hold out a whole value of Pm?' (the configured split holds out single points, Re 100 Pm 1 and Re 50 Pm 2, so every Pm keeps training data and criterion (c) is untestable); 10.9 'Can we get VKS and precession snapshots, in what format, and when?'. Question card ch10.Q (n 11 if ch09.Q is Q10; category runs; ask Y. Ponty): forcing, Reynolds-number definition and resolution of the Taylor-Green campaign, so that its threshold can be compared with the published one; it does not repeat Q3 (which Pm) or Q4 (spread or pack the points). REQUESTS. (1) tools/data_cloud.py (foundation engineer B): the result variants use 'when': 'met' | 'not_met' | 'inconclusive'; please add these three booleans to every converter's 'fields' (exactly one true); without them the conditional sentences drop and only the 'Verdict: {{verdict}}' sentence remains (safe). 10.9 needs 'vks_verdict' and 'dresdyn_verdict' in the fields of the generic seat JSONs tier3_vks.json and tier4_dresdyn.json. (2) tools/data_existing.py: NEW data/fm3d_guarantees.json for 10.6 (milady/train/fm3d.py decoder and B-sign-symmetrised velocity field with random weights, CPU, seconds, no simulation or training: div_rel_u, div_rel_b, mirror_error, packed field-line polylines of one sample, meta.stamp 'GENERATED · fm3d · untrained weights'); torch is not installed in the system python here, so it needs the repository venv; until the file exists the assembler renders 10.6 as pending with a warning. (3) tools/assemble_cut.py lints a result variant against the pending target_s; result targets are given in variants.result.target_s (10.4 45, 10.5 45, 10.7 40, 10.9 40, 10.3 15): 10.7 (about 41 s vs 25) will warn unless the lint reads that field. (4) conv_fm3d_eval lamp (b) uses err_spectre_*_log10, a mean over all shells, while T:917 asks 'per band up to half the cutoff' (stricter): the lamp may read 'met' where the plan would not. CHANGES AGAINST THE OUTLINE. 10.5: the outline chip said 'different forcing convention'; Ponty et al. 2005 (checked on arXiv physics/0410046) use the same Taylor-Green forcing shape at k0 = 2 but define R_V from the r.m.s. velocity and the integral scale, while palier2_tg3d uses U_ref = 1 and L_ref = 1/kf: narration and chip say 'defines the Reynolds number differently'. 10.4: confidence medium, because at 32³ the whole-run and last-quarter fits already disagree at Rm 18 (|s − s_q| > |s|), which the converter would call inconclusive. 10.2: the H6 stamp sentence becomes the grey seat tag (no provisional stamps under D4); badge MEASURED refers to the test suite only (consistency editor: confirm or change). 10.3: P for the injection rate and ε for the dissipation, as in ch08 (outline wrote eps_inj); the converter gives ONE j tile, not 11, so the strips carry the per-η information; the bet is a data check, labelled as not a PhD-plan criterion. 10.1: chapter card in the 3.2-s lead-in, rail holds at L4 (the chapter reaches L5 at 10.5). Cuts: 10.8 and 10.9 'cuts': ['core']; 10.9-bridge 'cuts': ['extended'] (outline extended_variant); ch10.Q closes the chapter in both cuts. No predict beat in this chapter (the outline lists none); 0.5-0.8-s holds after the bet paragraphs let the seat column be read. No new lexicon entry (Rm, Pm, VKS, DRESDYN, Reynolds, Rice are pinned; 'eta' is avoided, 'diffusivities' is said instead). Words budgeted at about 128 effective words per minute of target_s, checked with the assembler formula (146 raw words per minute, 0.9 s per paragraph break, holds, lead-in, tail). REVIEW 2026-11-08 (adversarial script review, see script/_review/ch10.md): (5) PRECISION (foundation engineer): the fm3d decoder works and returns float32 (milady/train/data.py to_grid, fm3d.py:782; tests/test_train.py:113 asserts relative divergence < 1e-6 in float32), so (i) data/fm3d_guarantees.json should decode in float64 (cast the decoder to double) and write meta.dtype, else the 10.6 gauge reads about 1e-7, and (ii) conv_fm3d_eval with div_tol 1e-12 will mark lamp (a) not_met on float32 samples: evaluate the divergence on a float64 decode, or set the tolerance to the dtype's rounding. (6) LAMP (b): err_spectre_*_log10 is the mean |log10 E_gen - log10 E_ref| over shells k = 1..8 (milady/eval/metrics.py:600, 630-639), and fm3d truncates at |m| <= 8: the ±0.1 band drawn around the curve is a guide, not the lamp's rule; the result narration no longer says 'every spectrum inside the band'. (7) CONTINUITY (consistency editor): chSOA2 (L4-L5) now precedes ch10 in both cuts (BRIEF §10); if it ends at L5, the 10.1 card's levelFrom 'L4' is a step down and needs the side-step treatment of ch08. New cues: 10.5 'push' and 'catch' (visual updated), 10.8 'nonlocal' (visual updated); sentence ids of 10.5 and 10.8 renumbered. scenes.title: The data factory

sentences.text: To climb, the study first built a factory for the data.
A recipe card sets the {param}knobs{/}.
Ovens run one simulation per setting, on a laptop or a cluster.
Each result is sealed in a labelled jar: a unique number, the code version, a checksum.
A ledger records every jar, a menu splits them for training and testing, the {model}chef{/} learns, and a {metric}critic{/} scores the result.
It all runs end to end on an ordinary processor, never yet on a graphics card or a real cluster.
A grey tag names the file each empty frame awaits.

labels: labelled jar · MFF file (HDF5, The Well)
chef in training · flow matching on potentials
grey tag = awaiting · filled tag = data with its checksum
chips: tested end to end on CPU (68 automated tests) · not yet run on a GPU or a real cluster

sentences.text: Bet one: the twisting box.
At thirty-two cubed, the small sweep matched the published windows, but near seventeen and a half the sign of growth stayed unresolved.
The campaign doubles the resolution and steps {param}Rm{/} by whole numbers up to forty.
The bet: growth still positive at seventeen, already negative at eighteen, with two fits agreeing: one over the kept part of the run, one over its last quarter.
Confidence: medium. At eighteen, the small sweep's two fits already differed by more than the rate itself.
Worth asking before the run: add three points between seventeen and eighteen?

formulas.tex: s(17) > 0 > s(18),\quad |s - s_q| < |s|\ \text{at } \Rm = 17 \text{ and } 18\quad (s_q:\ \text{fit over the last quarter; whole values of } \Rm)

sentences.text: Bet two, the first true dynamo: a Taylor-Green flow of counter-rotating eddies.
Now the {b}field{/} pushes back on the {u}flow{/}.
Above a threshold, a tiny {b}seed{/} should grow, then level off.
Twelve runs cross four Reynolds numbers with three values of {param}Pm{/}.
The bet: a threshold in {param}Rm{/}, bracketed for at least two values of {param}Pm{/}.

formulas.tex: E_B(t) \propto e^{2 s t}\ \text{(kinematic phase), then nonlinear saturation};\quad \Rm = \RE \times \PM
\text{here } \RE = U_{\rm ref} L_{\rm ref}/\nu,\ L_{\rm ref} = 1/k_f = 0.5;\ \text{Ponty et al. 2005: } R_V = U_{\rm rms} L/\nu,\ L = 2\pi \textstyle\int k^{-1}E(k)\,dk \big/ \int E(k)\,dk
\text{saturated if } |\text{slope of } \ln E_B \text{ over the kept window}|/2 < 0.1\, s_{\rm kin}\ \ (\text{saturation flag of the data converter})

scenes.title: Walls and iron

iron.kink_profile: potential across the interface: smooth (C1) vs kinked (|d|)

sentences.text: Leave the periodic box for a real vessel, and exact gets harder.
The potential needs a gauge and a wall condition; then each {b}field{/} has exactly one.
At the soft-iron impellers, {b}field lines{/} bend sharply at the iron's surface, so a smooth potential cannot be exact: it needs a kink there.
Outside, the {b}field{/} must match a current-free field in the vacuum.
The rule is linear but nonlocal: the {b}field{/} at one point of the wall depends on the whole wall.
Imposing it exactly and cheaply, for every sample, is still open.

question.en: Before the *Taylor–Green* runs: which forcing, Reynolds definition and resolution make their threshold *comparable* with published ones?
question.say: Before the Taylor-Green runs, which forcing, Reynolds number definition and resolution make their threshold comparable with published ones?
question.fr: Avant les simulations Taylor–Green : quel forçage, quelle définition du nombre de Reynolds et quelle résolution rendent leur seuil comparable aux seuils publiés ?
question.why: Bet 2 and the 3D generator's data come from this campaign; our Reynolds numbers use other scales than the published Rm_c = 30, and 64³ may be too coarse at Re ≥ 100.
question.unblocks: The settings of palier2_tg3d before renting: forcing amplitude, Re definition, grid (64³, or 128³ at Re ≥ 100); hence the threshold check of Bet 2 and the 3D training data.
question.why_fr: Le pari 2 et les données du générateur 3D viennent de cette campagne ; nos nombres de Reynolds utilisent d'autres échelles que le Rm_c = 30 publié, et 64³ risque d'être trop grossier à Re ≥ 100.
question.unblocks_fr: Les réglages de palier2_tg3d avant de louer : amplitude du forçage, définition de Re, grille (64³, ou 128³ à Re ≥ 100) ; donc la vérification du seuil du pari 2 et les données d'entraînement 3D.
